title: Odd-parity surface magnetism in a Kondo insulator
abstract: We formulate a theory of spin-polarized tunneling between a nanowire tip of a topological Kondo insulator SmB$_6$ and the bi-collinear antiferromagnet Fe$_{1+x}$Te in which the tunneling conductance which measures magnetic contrast changes sign when the bias is reversed. First we show that no time reversal symmetric tip, however strong its spin-momentum locking is, can produce experimentally observed magnetic contrast, which implies that time reversal must be broken at the tip surface. Within a mean-field treatment of the surface theory of SmB$_6$ we find that the interaction between conduction d-and f-electrons drives a surface phase transition near T$_c$ ~10 K in which the time reversal odd component of the Kondo hybridization amplitude condenses in the same symmetry channel as an out-of-plane surface magnetization, gapping out the Dirac surface states. Below the transition the spin-resolved spectral function of each gapped surface Dirac cone is odd in energy about its node. For a charge-neutral apex the Fermi level lies between the surface $Γ$ and $X$ Dirac nodes, so the spin-polarized conductance, which is determined by this function at the bias energy, reverses its sign close to zero bias. This sign change is thus a spectroscopic signature of time reversal symmetry breaking on the surface of SmB6.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to explain magnetic contrast observed in tunneling spectroscopy of Kondo insulators. It shows that the required sign change in conductance necessitates the breaking of time-reversal symmetry at the surface. This symmetry breaking is linked to the condensation of an odd-parity order parameter, providing a unique spectroscopic fingerprint of magnetism driven by electronic correlations.
main_problem: To theoretically explain the experimentally observed sign change in the tunneling conductance (magnetic contrast) when the bias voltage is reversed in a Kondo insulator junction.
main_result: The sign change is a spectroscopic signature of Time-Reversal Symmetry Breaking (TRSB) on the $	ext{SmB}_6$ surface, driven by the condensation of a time-reversal-odd order parameter ($\Delta P_T$).
method: The authors use a mean-field theory applied to the surface electronic structure, analyzing the spectral function and tunneling current using time-reversal symmetry decomposition.
model_or_system: The system involves a topological Kondo insulator ($	ext{SmB}_6$) nanowire tip tunneling into a bi-collinear antiferromagnet ($	ext{Fe}_{1+x}	ext{Te}$). The theory models the interaction between conduction $d$- and localized $f$-electrons.
key_observables: Tunneling conductance, which exhibits a sign change near zero bias voltage ($\delta I_{	ext{odd}}$).
important_parameters: Transition temperature $T_c \approx 10 	ext{ K}$; the time-reversal-odd hybridization amplitude $\Delta P_T$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the substrate magnetic pattern is perfectly commensurate and collinear, and the tunneling process is treated perturbatively.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the necessity of TRSB to explain the magnetic contrast, develops a mean-field theory for the $	ext{SmB}_6$ surface, predicts the condensation of the odd-parity order parameter $\Delta P_T$, and finally links this condensation to the sign reversal in the spin-polarized conductance.
why_interesting: The mechanism relies on the interplay between topological surface states, symmetry breaking (TRSB), and strong electronic correlations ($d-f$ hybridization), which are central themes in advanced condensed matter theory.
